messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: Latent residuals/mixture components
messages.body_plain:
The difficulty occurs because x1,x2,x3 are observed without error, right?

As a simple hack one can use
x1 = z + lx1 + e1
x2 = z + lx2  + e2
x3 = z + lx3   + e3

where ei ~ Normal(0,s), where "s" is a small quantity. Then the model has a straight forward implementation along the lines you have tried.

This does only approximately give the model you want. I am not aware of SEM implementations in TMB,
so I do not have other solutions to point to.

Hans

messages.subject: Weird issue with TMB objective function output... not changing when it should be?
messages.subject_clean: Weird issue with TMB objective function output... not changing when it should be?
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I've been working on a rather complicated likelihood function using TMB and I'm not getting the output I expected. Basically, the function's value doesn't change at all when I change one of the parameters even though it should. I'm almost positive that I wrote the function correctly (although, of course, I could be wrong) because I reported the value that is supposed to be returned (val in the code below) and it's different than what is returned by L_tau$fn. Notice here that I call L_tau with two different values of the fourth parameter and the first one (approximately the likelihood value identified by the MLE) is roughly accurate, but the second call should have a higher value and instead returns the same value. This of course means that I won't be able to identify the true optimal value of the fourth parameter. It even acknowledges that I've changed the fourth parameter, because tau is reported as different values in each function call.

> L_tau$fn(c(1.19, 1.28, 0.14, 100))
[1] 1141.93
> L_tau$report()
$tau
[1] 100

$angularconcentration
[1] 1.28

$dist_coef
[1] 0.14

$steplength
[1] 1.19

$val
[1] 1141.93

> L_tau$fn(c(1.19, 1.28, 0.14, 250))
[1] 1141.93
> L_tau$report()
$tau
[1] 250

$angularconcentration
[1] 1.28

$dist_coef
[1] 0.14

$steplength
[1] 1.19

$val
[1] 1278.448

I can attach the C++ code if that would be helpful but it's a large file so I figure including a massive script in this post would be a little onerous. I'm not sure if something like this has been encountered before (it probably has, but I only conducted a brief search), so let me know if anyone has any thoughts/recommendations! I'm rather new to TMB and C++ in general but quite experienced in R, so there could be something I'm not understanding correctly.

Thanks,
Peter

messages.subject: accuracy of the Laplace approximation
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a couple general questions about the accuracy of the Laplace approximation. I primarily work with GLMM spatial models where random effects follow a GMRF and data follow a variety of distributions such as delta-Gamma, Poisson, and Tweedie.

I run the checkConsistency function on my models and get high marginal p-values. This test, however, only considers the expectations of the joint and marginal. Are there any new developments in TMB that check the 2nd order accuracy or improve the approximation in the tails? If the marginal p-value from the test is high and parameter bias low, how concerned do I need to be about higher order inaccuracies?

I appreciate any feedback!
Andrea
